rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawā literally means falling from a height; here it metaphorically denotes irreversible ruin, with the threatened fall specified as from a mountain or roof and Qur'an 101:9 as a parallel.
rows.anchor: وهوى : سقط من علو ، وقد استعير هنا للهلاك الذي لا نهوض بعده ، كما قالوا : هوت أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of forgiveness is a digression after warning against excess in blessings, showing repentance and righteous action as remedies if excess occurs.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وإني لغفار } إلى آخرها استطراد بعد التحذير من الطغيان في النعمة بالإرشاد إلى ما يتدارك به الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance here means regretting disbelief, then believing and doing righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { تاب } : ندم على كفره وآمن وعمل صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks a difference in rank rather than time, and guidance means remaining firm and continuing on the path.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ثم اهتدى } ( ثم ) فيه للتراخي في الرتبة ؛ استعيرت للدلالة على التباين بين الشيئين في المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of continuing in guidance parallels the description of believers who say God is their Lord and then remain steadfast.
rows.anchor: فهو كقوله تعالى : إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses allude to Exodus's description of God as merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abundantly kind, forgiving sin yet not acquitting completely.
rows.anchor: والآيات تشير إلى ما جاء في الإصحاح من سفر الخروج ( الرب إله رحيم ورؤوف ، بطيء الغضب وكثير الإحسان غافر الإثم والخطيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about Moses's haste continues the command to travel with God's servants and explains the earlier revelation; this Sinai episode in the third month after leaving Egypt is omitted from al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { اسر بعبادي } ( طه : 77 ) الواقعة تفسيرا لفعل { أوحينا إلى موسى } ( طه : 77 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿjāl means making something occur sooner; the question is used as reproach.
rows.anchor: والإعجال : جعل الشيء عاجلا . والاستفهام مستعمل في اللوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes infer that Moses hurried ahead of his people to the meeting before God's appointed time, eager to receive the law as promised before Israel reached Sinai.
rows.anchor: أن موسى تعجل مفارقة قومه ليحضر إلى المناجاة قبل الإبان الذي عينه الله له ، اجتهادا منه ورغبة في تلقي الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reproached Moses for neglecting care for his people by leaving before they were instructed to keep the covenant and warned against a suspected schemer.
rows.anchor: فلامه الله على أن غفل عن مراعاة ما يحف بذلك من ابتعاده عن قومه قبل أن يوصيهم الله بالمحافظة على العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's haste is likened to Abu Bakr finding the Prophet bowing in the mosque, bowing himself, then moving into the row.
rows.anchor: فكان في ذلك بمنزلة أبي بكر حين دخل المسجد فوجد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم راكعا فركع ودب إلى الصف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the cited report, the Prophet responded to Abu Bakr's hurried action by wishing him greater eagerness and telling him not to repeat it.
rows.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( زادك الله حرصا ولا تعد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about breaking Moses's appointment follows from the second rhetorical, rejecting question.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فأخلفتم موعدي } تفريع على الاستفهام الإنكاري الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's appointment means God's promise conveyed through him; it is attributed to Moses because he was the intermediary.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { موعدي } هو وعد الله على لسانه ، فإضافته إلى ضميره لأنه الواسطة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the verb for scattering stresses that the mountains' destruction is literal, not metaphorical; the statement answers those asking the Prophet about mountains.
rows.anchor: وأكد { ينسفها نسفا } لإثبات أنه حقيقة لا استعارة . فتقدير الكلام : ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasf means scattering and dispersing into dust, a meaning explained earlier.
rows.anchor: والنسف : تفريق وإذراء ، وتقدم آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qāʿ is level, easy land, while al-ṣafṣaf is even ground without raised places.
rows.anchor: والقاع : الأرض السهلة . والصفصف : الأرض المستوية التي لا نتوء فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are crushed in place and leveled to the surrounding ground, through an earthquake or something similar, as another Qur'anic description says.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { يذرها قاعا صفصفا } أنها تندك في مواضعها وتسوى مع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause denying crookedness or elevation is a circumstantial clause that reinforces flatness and makes the scene more vivid and frightening.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا } حال مؤكدة لمعنى { قاعا صفصفا } لزيادة تصوير حالة فيزيد تهويلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person address is to no particular person; it includes the Prophet and those who asked about the mountains.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في { لا ترى فيها عوجا } لغير معين يخاطب به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم سائليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest linguistic view treats ʿawaj with either vowel pattern as synonymous; this is the position attributed to ʿAmr and chosen by al-Marzūqī.
rows.anchor: فهما مترادفان على الصحيح من أقوال أيمة اللغة

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: One group says kasra describes non-upright bodies such as land and abstract things, while fatḥa describes upright objects; Ibn al-Azharī's wording in Lisān al-ʿArab appears to support this distinction.
rows.anchor: وقال جماعة : مكسور العين يجري على الأجسام غير المنتصبة كالأرض وعلى الأشياء المعنوية

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Another distinction assigns kasra to abstract meanings and fatḥa to concrete entities; Ibn Durayd reports it and al-Kashshāf follows it.
rows.anchor: وهذا أضعف الأقوال . وهو منقول عن ابن دريد في ( الجمهرة ) وتبعه في ( الكشاف ) هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the abstract/concrete distinction the weakest view and says al-Kashshāf forced the verse away from its apparent sense, wrongly restricting how the word may be used.
rows.anchor: وهذا أضعف الأقوال . وهو منقول عن ابن دريد في ( الجمهرة ) وتبعه في ( الكشاف ) هنا ، وكأنه مال إلى ما فيه من التفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿawaj was discussed at the opening of Sūrat al-Kahf as well.
rows.anchor: وتقدم هذا اللفظ في أول سورة الكهف فانظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amt means a slight protrusion, so the land has neither a hollow nor any raised bump.
rows.anchor: والأمت : النتوء اليسير ، أي لا ترى فيها وهدة ولا نتوءا ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the caller results from the mountains being scattered: once they are crushed, people are summoned to resurrection and follow toward the gathering place.
rows.anchor: جملة { يتبعون الداعي } في معنى المفرعة على جملة { ينسفها } ( طه : 105 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawmئidh is an adverb attached to following the caller; placing it first emphasizes that day and supplies a connective transition, meaning the day the mountains are scattered.
rows.anchor: و { يومئذ } ظرف متعلق ب { يتبعون الداعي } . وقدم الظرف على عامله للاهتمام بذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the caller as the angel Isrāfīl, whose compelling creative summons restores bodies and souls and draws them to the appointed place.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو الملك إسرافيل عليه السلام يدعو بنداء التسخير والتكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the caller as each people's messenger, whom that people follows.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الداعي الرسول ، أي يتبع كل قوم رسولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase denying crookedness is circumstantial; under either caller interpretation, people do not veer but head directly toward the caller's destination.
rows.anchor: و { عوج له } حال من { الداعي } . واللام على كلا القولين في المراد من الداعي للأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the caller is a messenger, crookedness can mean falsehood, alluding to polytheists' slander that the Prophet was bewitched or deviant.
rows.anchor: ويجيء على قول من جعل المراد بالداعي الرسول أن يراد بالعوج الباطل تعريضا بالمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun's negation excludes every kind of crookedness in following the caller: no one takes another way, is led by another way, or knows his messenger to be crooked.
rows.anchor: فالمصدر المنفي أريد منه نفي جنس العوج في اتباع الداعي ، بحيث لا يسلكون غير الطريق القويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matching denials of crookedness connect the flat earth with the straight path people take across it; they do not evade or deviate, as in the description of the resurrection plain.
rows.anchor: وبين قوله { لا ترى فيها عوجا } ( طه : 107 ) وقوله { لا عوج له } مراعاة النظير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushūʿ means submission; its manifestation in a voice is speaking softly, which explains why only whispers are heard.
rows.anchor: والخشوع : الخضوع ، وفي كل شيء من الإنسان مظهر من الخشوع ؛ فمظهر الخشوع في الصوت : الإسرار به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hams is a faint, quiet sound.
rows.anchor: والهمس : الصوت الخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person address about seeing no crookedness and hearing only whispers is generic, referring to any observer or listener.
rows.anchor: والخطاب بقوله { لا ترى فيها عوجا وقوله فلا تسمع إلا همسا خطاب لغير معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the voices humble is a rational metaphor because their speakers are humble; alternatively, humility is borrowed to mean low, hushed sound, all from the dread of the scene.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الخشوع إلى الأصوات مجاز عقلي ، فإن الخشوع لأصحاب الأصوات ؛ أو استعير الخشوع لانخفاض الصوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial that intercession benefits anyone follows from the whispering scene: people barely speak and dare not intercede for those they hope to help.
rows.anchor: وجملة يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة } كجملة { يومئذ يتبعون الداعي } في معنى التفريع على { وخشعت الأصوات للرحمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's majesty and fear prevent intercession except by permission, frustrating polytheists' hope of finding intercessors with God.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا أن جلال الله والخشية منه يصدان عن التوسط عنده لنفع أحد إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception referring to one God permits is complete: intercession entails an intercessor, so it means an intercessor permitted by the Merciful to intercede.
rows.anchor: واستثناء { من أذن له الرحمان } من عموم الشفاعة باعتبار أن الشفاعة تقتضي شافعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in permission is a preposition that makes the verb transitive, as in Pharaoh's statement; the Prophet's intercession report explains the meaning.
rows.anchor: واللام في { أذن له } لام تعدية فعل { أذن } ، مثل قوله { قال فرعون آمنتم به قبل أن آذن لكم }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the intercession report, God tells the Prophet to ask and he will be granted, and to intercede and his intercession will be accepted.
rows.anchor: وتفسير هذا ما ورد في حديث الشفاعة من قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( فيقال لي : سل تعطه واشفع تشفع )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the approval clause refers back to the person God permitted to intercede, namely the intercessor.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ورضي له قولا } عائد إلى { من أذن له الرحمان وهو الشافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām means that God approves the intercessor's words for his sake, honoring him; permission entails the intention to accept the intercession and signals the intercessor's rank.
rows.anchor: واللام الداخلة على ذلك الضمير لام التعليل ، أي رضي الرحمان قول الشافع لأجل الشافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawlan is accusative as the direct object of raḍiya, which can take the approved matter directly or with bi.
rows.anchor: والمجرور متعلق بفعل { رضي } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God knows what is before and behind people explains why He approves those for whom intercession is permitted: His knowledge encompasses outward deeds and hidden inner states.
rows.anchor: وجملة يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم } مستأنفة بيانية لجواب سؤال من قد يسأل بيان ما يوجب رضى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is before people represents visible deeds, and what is behind them represents concealed secrets, by metaphorical reference to what is in front of or behind someone.
rows.anchor: فعبر عن الأعمال الظاهرة بما بين أيديهم لأن شأن ما بين الأيدي أن يكون واضحا ، وعبر عن السرائر بما خلفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanation appeared earlier in Āyat al-Kursī.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم ذلك في آية الكرسي ، فهو كناية عن الظاهرات والخفيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says intercession may rescue groups who have even a mustard-seed's weight of faith from Hell.
rows.anchor: مثل ما ورد في الحديث ( يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من إيمان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report describes the supreme intercession at the gathering, seeking the reckoning of all people to begin sooner.
rows.anchor: أو بأن يشفع في حالة خاصة مثل ما ورد في حديث الشفاعة العظمى في الموقف لجميع الناس بتعجيل حسابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that people cannot encompass God with knowledge concludes by emphasizing His immense knowledge and the smallness of human knowledge, as in Āyat al-Kursī.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ولا يحيطون به علما } تذييل للتعليم بعظمة علم الله تعالى وضآلة علم البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces' abasement parallels the voices' humility; ʿanā means humiliation and originally captivity, with an imprisoned person called ʿānī.
rows.anchor: والعناء : الذلة ، وأصله الأسر ، والعاني : الأسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Assigning abasement to faces is a rational metaphor, and the whole scene depicts the criminals described earlier as blue-eyed.
rows.anchor: والجملة كلها تمثيل لحال المجرمين الذين الكلام عليهم من قوله { ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ رزقا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in faces substitutes for a possessive, meaning their faces, as in the statement that Hell is the refuge.
rows.anchor: فاللام في { الوجوه عوض عن المضاف إليه ، أي وجوههم ، كقوله تعالى : فإن الجحيم هي المأوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, the faces of the obedient will be laughing and radiant.
rows.anchor: وأما وجوه أهل الطاعات فهي وجوه يومئذ ضاحكة مستبشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is built around establishing Muhammad's prophethood and validating his call: it opens with warning and proof, notes that he is not an unprecedented messenger, then gives examples of earlier prophets amid exhortations and evidence.
rows.anchor: أقيمت هذه السورة على عماد إثبات الرسالة لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وتصديق دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse gathers the preceding accounts of prophets given judgment, knowledge, and honors, describing Muhammad's mission as distinctively universal and enduring mercy; it closes their virtues, while the intervening material is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وعطفت هذه الجملة على جميع ما تقدم من ذكر الأنبياء الذين أوتوا حكما وعلما وذكر ما أوتوه من الكرامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also connects to the earlier challenge in which wrongdoers whisper that Muhammad is merely a human being and call his message sorcery.
rows.anchor: ولهذه الجملة اتصال بآية { وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم أفتأتون السحر وأنتم تبصرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its description of Muhammad's law as mercy parallels descriptions of what Moses, Aaron, and Abraham received.
rows.anchor: ووزانها في وصف شريعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وزان آية : { ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's twelve specific rhetorical meanings exceed the six gathered in the famous opening poetic line, which says stop, calls for stopping, weep, calls for weeping, and names a beloved and a dwelling.
rows.anchor: إذ تلك الكلمة قصاراها كما قالوا : ( أنه وقف واستوقف وبكى واستبكى وذكر الحبيب والمنزل ) دون خصوصية أزيد من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the poem, indefinite beloved and dwelling indicate one particular person and place: the beloved associated with that dwelling and his own home.
rows.anchor: وليس تنكير ( حبيب ومنزل ) إلا للوحدة لأنه أراد فردا معينا من جنس الأحباب وفردا معينا من جنس المنازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parsing mercy as a circumstantial predicate of the addressee, together with restriction, makes this a restriction of the Messenger to the attribute of mercy: his whole existence and every state are mercy.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن انتصاب { رحمة } على أنه حال من ضمير المخاطب يجعله وصفا من أوصافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the verbal noun intensifies the union of mercy with his mission; the Prophet expressed this as being a mercy bestowed.
rows.anchor: ووقوع الوصف مصدرا يفيد المبالغة في هذا الاتحاد بحيث تكون الرحمة صفة متمكنة من إرساله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet described himself as a mercy granted by God.
rows.anchor: ويدل لهذا المعنى ما أشار إلى شرحه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله : ( إنما أنا رحمة مهداة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's mercy appears in two ways: the Prophet's own character and the mercy built into the law he brought.
rows.anchor: وتفصيل ذلك يظهر في مظهرين : الأول تخلق نفسه الزكية بخلق الرحمة ، والثاني إحاطة الرحمة بتصاريف شريعته

rows.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن طاهر القيسي الإشبيلي
rows.claim: Ibn Ṭāhir says God adorned Muhammad with mercy, so his existence, character, and attributes were mercy to creation; ʿIyāḍ quotes this in al-Shifāʾ.
rows.anchor: فقد قال فيه أبو بكر محمد بن طاهر القيسي الإشبيلي أحد تلاميذه أبي علي الغساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that Muhammad was naturally merciful in all dealings with his community, fitting him to receive a revealed law of mercy that matched his character and desires.
rows.anchor: قلت : يعني أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فطر على خلق الرحمة في جميع أحوال معاملته الأمة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha characterized the Prophet's conduct as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة : ( كان خلقه القرآن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an singles Muhammad out for the description of mercy, supported by the descriptions of his compassion to believers and his gentleness with them.
rows.anchor: ولهذا خص الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه السورة بوصف الرحمة ولم يصف به غيره من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After the Prophet was wounded at Uḥud, companions asked him to invoke against his enemies; he replied that he was sent as mercy, not as a curser.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث مسلم : أن رسول الله لما شج وجهه يوم أحد شق ذلك على أصحابه فقالوا : لو دعوت عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second manifestation of mercy is the law's provisions that make it broadly merciful to all creation; the phrase for all worlds modifies mercy.
rows.anchor: وأما المظهر الثاني من مظاهر كونه رحمة للعالمين فهو مظهر تصاريف شريعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural al-ʿālamīn covers every class called a world, meaning either rational beings (humans) or kinds of living creatures, as in the opening of Sūrat al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { العالمين } لاستغراق كل ما يصدق عليه اسم العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase means human communities, Islamic law is more comprehensively merciful than earlier laws because it addresses people's circumstances broadly.
rows.anchor: فإن أريد أصناف ذوي العلم فمعنى كون الشريعة المحمدية منحصرة في الرحمة أنها أوسع الشرائع رحمة بالناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's ḥanīfī law and Jesus's law were individually focused rather than general legislation, whereas the Torah covered more personal and communal circumstances.
rows.anchor: فالحنيفية شريعة إبراهيم عليه السلام كانت رحمة خاصة بحالة الشخص في نفسه وليس فيها تشريع عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the Torah was a mercy, many of its penalties required sustained hardship as a divinely wise policy for its people.
rows.anchor: وهي رحمة كما وصفها الله بذلك في قوله تعالى : { ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب تماما على الذي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam's law is uniquely complete in mercy; God's promise that mercy encompasses everything and is written for those who follow the unlettered Messenger indicates its universality beyond one nation.
rows.anchor: لا جرم أن الله تعالى خص الشريعة الإسلامية بوصف الرحمة الكاملة . وقد أشار إلى ذلك قوله تعالى فيما حكاه خطابا منه لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's changing conditions eventually made people ready to be governed with mercy and relieved of hardship except when necessary; earlier mixtures of mercy and severity and Islam's lasting mercy both reflect wisdom, while Islam arrived at the fitting stage.
rows.anchor: وحكمة تمييز شريعة الإسلام بهذه المزية أن أحوال النفوس البشرية مضت عليها عصور وأطوار تهيأت بتطوراتها لأن تساس بالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic law rests on mercy, gentleness, and ease, as shown by the declarations that religion has no hardship and that God intends ease, and by the Prophetic description of tolerant ḥanīfī religion.
rows.anchor: فأقيمت شريعة الإسلام على دعائم الرحمة والرفق واليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation and fixed penalties may seem harsh, but they balance hardship to offenders against mercy to everyone else, as the verse about life through retaliation states.
rows.anchor: وما يتخيل من شدة في نحو القصاص والحدود فإنما هو لمراعاة تعارض الرحمة والمشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam's mercy to non-Muslim communities under Muslim rule means no coercion to leave their religions and equal justice in general rights and duties.
rows.anchor: وأما رحمة الإسلام بالأمم غير المسلمين فإنما نعني به رحمته بالأمم الداخلة تحت سلطانه وهم أهل الذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-ʿālamīn means living kinds, the law's care for animals falls within mercy because animals are created for human use, as the cited passages explain.
rows.anchor: هذا وإن أريد ب { العالمين } في قوله تعالى : { إلا رحمة للعالمين } النوع من أنواع المخلوقات ذات الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law permits people to benefit from animals in useful ways and does not authorize other treatment.
rows.anchor: وقد أذنت الشريعة الإسلامية للناس في الانتفاع بما ينتفع به من الحيوان ولم تأذن في غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recreational hunting is disliked and harming animals outside the purpose of eating them is forbidden; jurists treat horse racing as a concession for military needs and similar purposes.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كره صيد اللهو وحرم تعذيب الحيوان لغير أكله ، وعد فقهاؤنا سباق الخيل رخصة للحاجة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ says God forgave a man who drew water from a well and gave it to a thirsty dog.
rows.anchor: ففي حديث ( الموطأ ) عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا : ( أن الله غفر لرجل وجد كلبا يلهث من العطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may kill or drive away harmful animals because protecting human beings takes precedence over mercy to beasts.
rows.anchor: أما المؤذي والمضر من الحيوان فقد أذن في قتله وطرده لترجيح رحمة الناس على رحمة البهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening restriction says that what is revealed about God is that He is one; the following restriction makes divine unity exclusive, allowing no plurality of gods.
rows.anchor: فقد أفادت أن صاحب هذه الحقيقة مستأثر بالوحدانية فلا يكون في هذه الحقيقة تعدد أفراد فأفادت قصرا ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first restriction is relative: what is revealed to Muhammad concerning divinity is only that God is one.
rows.anchor: والقصر الأول إضافي ، أي ما يوحى إلي في شأن الإله إلا أن الإله إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second restriction is also relative, addressing God's oneness specifically; both restrictions answer the polytheists' beliefs.
rows.anchor: والقصر الثاني أيضا إضافي ، أي في شأن الإله من حيث الوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first restriction rejects the claim that Muhammad's appeal to both Allah and the Merciful contradicts monotheism, as well as the charge that he is a sorcerer for teaching an incomprehensible doctrine.
rows.anchor: فالقصر الأول لإبطال ما يلبسون به على الناس من أن محمدا يدعو إلى التوحيد ثم يذكر الله والرحمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The message also means Muhammad is no unprecedented messenger and echoes the challenge to ask earlier messengers whether other gods were appointed besides the Merciful.
rows.anchor: فيكون معنى الآية في معنى قوله تعالى : { قل ما كنت بدعا من الرسل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together the two restrictions concisely express Islam's call and lead to the question asking whether the audience will submit.
rows.anchor: ثم إن كلا القصرين كان كلمة جامعة لدعوة الإسلام تقريبا لشقة الخلاف والتشعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether they will submit after the explanation and also urges them to abandon idolatry and enter Islam.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام حقيقي ، أي فهل تسلمون بعد هذا البيان . وهو مستعمل أيضا في معنى كنائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The participle denotes the present, expressing impatience at their delayed conversion.
rows.anchor: واسم الفاعل مستعمل في الحال على أصله ، أي فهل أنتم مسلمون الآن استبطاء لتأخر إسلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence asks for stable submission rather than a passing act and hints that the audience remains doubtful and wavering.
rows.anchor: وصيغ ذلك في الجملة الاسمية الدالة على الثبات دون أن يقال : فهل تسلمون ، لإفادة أن المطلوب منهم إسلام ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away after this detailed, comprehensive clarification, the Prophet is to warn them that the promised punishment will arrive.
rows.anchor: أي فإن أعرضوا بعد هذا التبيين المفصل والجامع فأبلغهم الإنذار بحلول ما توعدهم الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised event includes every threatened punishment in this world and the next, whether the disbelievers remain alive or die.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون } يشمل كل ما يوعدونه من عقاب في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this clause in is negative; the interrogative particle suspends adrī from taking its complement, and the omitted relative pronoun is understood as what they are promised with.
rows.anchor: و ( إن ) نافية وعلق فعل { أدري } عن العمل بسبب حرف الاستفهام وحذف العائد . وتقديره : ما توعدون به
